The SHUSH Act's inclusion in the OBBBA is a critical step toward restoring constitutional rights. Eliminating the $200 tax stamp on suppressors—a relic of 1934’s overreach—correctly treats these hearing protection devices as standard accessories, not NFA items. With 4.86 million suppressors legally owned and near-zero crime linkage (ATF data), this reform aligns with reality.

But let’s not pretend the job’s done. The Hearing Protection Act’s full passage remains essential to dismantle all bureaucratic barriers.

Defending the Second Amendment means rejecting all unjustified taxes and registrations—not just trimming them.

The Firearms Policy Coalition’s lawsuit against interstate handgun bans proves the feds also weaponize red tape to restrict rights. When agencies drag their feet or impose illegal hurdles, they’re not enforcing laws—they’re violating the Constitution.

Defend the right, dismantle the bureaucracy.
